title: The Lawyers' Timeshare
teaser: Two lawyers, two clients, one mailbox and a whole lot of invoices.

news.headline: The Billboard War
news.body: Marty Kessler-Vance and Gloria Szabo-Reyes have the two loudest ads in Queens and, allegedly, its coldest rivalry. Within an hour of the first diss track, both of them were dialing.
news.hook: Marty's voicemail to Lord Menace, 12:21 AM: "You need representation. Also, do you need representation?"
news.post:
Roommates, before this beef has lawsuits, it has lawyers, and I need you to meet them properly, because they're about to be very busy.

If you drive in Queens, you know Marty Kessler-Vance. He's the face on the expressway billboard, forty feet wide, pointing at traffic: "INSULTED? CALL MARTY." Silver hair, big teeth, a tie the color of a traffic cone. He's been up there since before some of y'all had phones.

If you take the bus, you know Gloria Szabo-Reyes. She's on every bus shelter in the borough, arms crossed, yellow letters: "SZABO SUES!" There's a jingle. Three notes. You're humming it now. I'm sorry.

These two have run a billboard war for years. When Marty went bigger on the expressway, Gloria went brighter on the shelters. When Gloria got a jingle, Marty got a second billboard facing the first one. Queens has always assumed they can't stand each other. They've never been photographed together. Not once. Mad suspicious, if you ask me, but nobody asked me. Yet.

Last night at midnight, Lord Menace dropped "Rental Car Ruckus." At 12:21 AM, according to a voicemail my source played for me, Marty called him. Not a text. A call. "Desmond, I mean, Mr. Menace, this is Marty. You need representation. Also, do you need representation? Call me. Day or night. Mostly night."

He said "Desmond." I'm noting it. I don't know what it means yet.

At 12:40 AM, Big Ruckus dropped "Retainer." At 12:58 AM, Ruckus got a voicemail too. Gloria, all business: "Mr. Ruckus. Gloria Szabo-Reyes. I've heard the song. You have a case. Against whom, we'll decide later."

"Against whom, we'll decide later," y'all. That's not legal advice, that's a vibe.

Neither lawyer has been hired. Yet. But both sent a "consultation summary" by email before breakfast. Same font. Same little scales-of-justice logo. Different letterheads.

I'm a gossip, Roommates, not a detective. But I know what two people competing for the same thing look like, and I know what two people in on the same thing look like, and I'm deadass not sure which one this is.

So tell me: Team Billboard or Team Bus Shelter? And which rapper picks up the phone first?

news.headline: Invoice No. 1
news.body: Lord Menace hired Marty. Big Ruckus hired Gloria. The first invoices are in, and they bill for things no human has ever billed for.
news.hook: Both invoices send payment to the same P.O. box. In Bayside.
news.post:
Roommates, money talks, and today it's talking in line items.

A source in a certain King of Steinway Street's business office sent me Marty Kessler-Vance's first invoice for the sandwich case. A source who does Big Ruckus's books sent me Gloria Szabo-Reyes's first invoice for the nail spa case. They're side by side on my kitchen table, and chile, I've had to get up and walk around twice.

Marty's highlights: "Review of chalkboard, in person, at the deli: 3 hours, C$2,400." "Purchase of one egg-white sandwich, for evidence: C$6. Eaten by counsel." "Research: is sodium defamatory? 4.5 hours, C$3,600." "Drafting the phrase 'sandwich-based character assassination': C$1,200."

Gloria's highlights: "Expert consultation, nail tech, Flushing: 2 hours, C$1,800." "Magnification of cuticles, both parties: C$900." "Composition of the phrase 'emotional, cuticular and reputational': C$1,500." "Jingle royalties (self): C$250."

Not her billing a client for her own jingle. We love a woman who knows her worth.

Combined, that's already over C$40,000, three days into this beef. Lord Menace's comment to my source: "Facts, you pay for quality." Big Ruckus's: "Whatever it takes." Neither of them has read his invoice. I can tell, because neither of them has fainted.

But here's what stopped me. At the bottom of each invoice there's a "Remit payment to" line. Marty's office is in Forest Hills. Gloria's is in Jamaica. And both invoices say to mail checks to the same P.O. box. In Bayside. Same number.

Now, there could be an innocent explanation. Maybe it's a mailing service. Maybe it's a lawyers' co-op. Maybe two rivals who have never been photographed together just love the same post office. I called the post office. The man said, "Lady, I can't tell you whose box it is." Then he said, "But they're very nice." Then he hung up.

They're very nice. They. Plural. I'm buggin'.

So tell me, Roommates: what's the most ridiculous thing you've ever been billed for? And should two rival lawyers ever share a P.O. box?

news.headline: Same Door, Same Second
news.body: Both lawyers served DJ Sharm Almight on air at the exact same moment. The hallway camera at Real Clout FM caught what happened at the elevator first.
news.hook: In the footage, Marty fixes Gloria's collar. She lets him.
news.post:
Roommates, by now you've seen the clip: Sharm says "I read shoutouts, not subpoenas," and Marty and Gloria walk through the studio door at the same second, envelopes up, like synchronized swimming with paperwork.

Everybody's asking the same question. How do two rival lawyers who supposedly can't stand each other arrive at the same door at the same second?

Well. Real Clout FM has a camera in the hallway, and the station's security guard, a loyal reader since day one (hi, Reggie), let me watch the footage from the elevator bank. I can't post it, but I can describe it.

7:42 AM: the elevator opens. Marty and Gloria step out. Together. They rode up in the same elevator. Also 7:42: Marty fixes Gloria's collar. She lets him. 7:43: Gloria hands Marty a mint. He takes it without looking, like he's taken a thousand of them. Then they split up and walk to opposite ends of the hallway. Gloria checks her watch. Marty checks his. 7:44: they each walk back toward the studio from opposite directions, envelopes out, faces serious, and arrive at the same second.

They rehearsed it, y'all. They rehearsed the coincidence.

Then came the invoices, obviously. Marty billed Lord Menace "service of process, live radio, premium time slot: C$4,000." Gloria billed Big Ruckus "service of process, live radio, with jingle: C$4,250." Sharm got two envelopes, a headache and the best ratings of his life. He told me, "Yo, I'm buggin', but I'm not tight. Bet they settle."

There's one more thing on that footage. When they got back in the elevator, right before the doors closed, Reggie swears Gloria rested her head on Marty's shoulder. For one second. Then the doors shut.

I'm not saying they're friends. I'm not saying they're more than friends. I'm saying the collar, the mint and the shoulder are three receipts, and I've built whole stories on less.

So tell me, Roommates: rehearsed or real? And what would you do if a lawyer handed you a mint?

news.headline: Billable Breeze
news.body: Married nineteen years, fired twice in one afternoon, and still closing on a beach timeshare. Lola has the brochure, the down payment and the name on the door.
news.hook: Gloria's misdialed voicemail: "Babe, we're fired. By both of them. Does the timeshare still have the pool towels?"
news.post:
Roommates, now that the whole borough knows Marty Kessler-Vance and Gloria Szabo-Reyes have been married for nineteen years, let's talk about the purchase at the bottom of all of this: the timeshare.

Rosalind, our hero mail carrier, says the brochure landed in their Bayside mailbox a couple of weeks ago, and the closing papers came this week. I have a copy of the brochure, because my cousin sells timeshares and she owes me.

The place is called Seabreeze Settlement Villas, two hours south, on the beach. A pool shaped like a seashell. A "lazy river," which, sis, is a slow pool. Their unit is 2B, "ocean view if you lean."

The down payment: C$86,450. So I did something petty. I added up every invoice our two rappers received in the first week of this beef. C$86,450. To the dollar.

And owners get a little plaque for the door. Theirs says: "BILLABLE BREEZE."

Then the firing. You know both rappers fired both lawyers, so each lawyer got fired twice in one afternoon. What you don't know is that each of them sent a final invoice for being fired. "Termination review, emotional: C$1,000." Both. Same amount. Same font.

And then there's the voicemail. Gloria meant to call Marty that night and called Big Ruckus by mistake, and Ruckus played it for me, cheesin' the whole time: "Babe, we're fired. Both of us. By both of them. Does the timeshare still have the pool towels? Also, pick up dinner."

Now, a lot of y'all voted that these two were behind @QueensReceipts, and I get it. Motive: every leak meant another lawsuit. But look at the receipts I've shown you all week. A shared P.O. box. One elevator. A collar, a mint, a shoulder. A misdialed "babe." These two couldn't keep their own marriage secret from a mail carrier. You think they ran an anonymous account for weeks without slipping? Fuhgeddaboudit. Greedy, yes. Organized, no.

So tell me, Roommates: would you buy a timeshare called Billable Breeze? And who do you think is really behind those receipts?

news.headline: The Couples' Discount
news.body: Marty and Gloria turned up holding hands to offer both rappers a couples' discount, after a joint voicemail to Toni went nowhere. Their final invoice is the best thing they've ever written.
news.hook: Last line of the last invoice: "Lessons learned: priceless. Billed anyway."
news.post:
Roommates, our favorite married litigators have officially stopped pretending, and honestly, it's the healthiest I've ever seen them.

Let's go back to yesterday, when Toni Treasure confessed to running the whole beef. Within the hour, Marty and Gloria left her a joint voicemail, both on the line at once: "Ms. Treasure, we'd be delighted to represent you going forward. Together. We have a family rate." Toni's reply, by text, in full: "I read my own contracts." Sis left them on read after that.

They also finally explained how they knew both legal names so fast. Two weeks ago, an unsigned envelope slid under each of their office doors. Marty's held a photo of a pharmacy bag with "D. PETTIBONE" on it. Gloria's held a photo of an oboe case with "G. FENNIMORE III" on the tag. Both envelopes smelled like vanilla body spray. They never asked who sent them. "We don't ask where things come from," Marty told me. "Like money."

Then this morning, outside Sal's, our two rappers called their joint press conference in matching robes and announced a joint lawsuit against Toni. Eleven minutes later, Marty and Gloria walked up holding hands and offered to take the case "at a couples' discount." You saw what happened next. The rappers looked at them, looked at the napkins framed in Sal's window and dropped the whole thing.

But not before the lawyers sent one final invoice, to "Desmond & Gerald, jointly." Line items: "Arriving holding hands: no charge." "Couples' discount: 10%." "Emotional growth, observed: C$500." And the last line: "Lessons learned: priceless. Billed anyway."

Where are they now? Seabreeze Settlement Villas, unit 2B, Billable Breeze. Gloria posted a photo from the lazy river: two inner tubes, two laptops, one caption, "working vacation 💼🌊." Deadass the most on-brand thing I've ever seen.

And the ads have changed. The expressway billboard and every bus shelter now show the same picture of the two of them, back to back, arms crossed, under four words: "WE SUE. TOGETHER." The jingle has a second verse now. It's a duet. I hate how catchy it is.

So tell me, Roommates: would you hire a married legal team? And who gets the remote at Billable Breeze?
